title: Appendix II: Creatures of the Inner Planes
audit_comment: APPENDIX II: CREATURES OF THE INNER PLANES, printed pp. 120-121, the elemental analogues: the inner planes natural environments to their inhabitants - elemental herbivores grazing on their surroundings, elemental carnivores preying on elemental (and normative) life, the DM adapting the Monster Manual, Monster Manual II and Fiend Folio stats. The no-analogue list: no Ethereal, Astral or outer-plane natives (slaad, githyanki, devils), no elemental undead (though Prime undead may visit), and none for the PC humanoids - no elemental wizards, though some elemental creatures cast. The stat modifications: movement tripled for Air, Smoke and Steam, doubled for Water; the lair percentage 10% lower in the native plane and 10% higher in elemental pockets elsewhere; AC, attacks, damage, frequency, number appearing, magic resistance, intelligence unchanged, alignment unchanged or neutral with tendencies, no psionics unless noted. The abilities: movement through the home plane and its adjoining para- and quasi-planes as Prime travelers move through the Ethereal, sight into the Border Ethereal, entry to the Ethereal - but no Prime crossing without outside help. The per-element rungs: Air immune to wind, weather, lightning and clouds, hurt by vacuum; Fire hurt by cold and water; Earth with the improved AC and the passwall; Water breathing and blending; Smoke, Magma, Ooze, Ice, Lightning, Radiance, Minerals, Steam, Vacuum, Ash, Dust and Salt each with the immunity and vulnerability as printed - and the fire giant of Ash keeping its immunity, for where the Prime creature's immunity is the analogue's vulnerability, the analogue retains it. The appearances: ninety percent of air creatures invisible, the rest from amorphous clouds to humanoid avians; the Fire die from flaming solids through orbiting 2d6 geometric swarms to the metallic-hide counterparts; Earth from boulders through xorn-like tripeds to crystalline forms that shatter into useless shards; the Water amoeboids, serpents, mer-creatures and fish; the para-elemental humanoids and counterparts with the printed splits; and the eight quasi-forms from the bolt-legged lightning balls to the salt-encrusted duplicates. The size-change table by family with the halving-and-doubling effects (the 15-foot giant's 60-foot equivalent); and the treasure: Air's 10% coinage in perfume, Fire's 20% in melted blocks or protected burnables, Earth's metal-and-gems preference, Water's doubled potions, the 50/50 para-rule, the seven-of-eight quasi-rule with Vacuum normal, the protection by low-intelligence keepers, and the elemental-pocket equivalence.

consts.name: ddyAirMoveMult
consts.comment: the elemental movement stat: triple the listed speed for creatures of the planes of Air, Smoke, or Steam; double the listed speed for creatures of Water; unchanged for all others - this being the physical distance the creatures can move in the inner planes, moving point to point as Prime planar travelers can in the Ethereal.

consts.name: ddyAirInvisiblePct
consts.comment: the air-creature appearance rule: ninety percent of air creatures encountered are invisible, though detectable by spell use or high intelligence - the remainder rolling on the appearance die: 1-10 amorphous cloud-like with grasping members from a churning center, 11-15 streamlined ellipsoid or arrow-head with arms from the center, 16-75 a narrow streamlined Prime counterpart with stubby fins, 76-90 the counterpart's form with long thin wings, 91-00 a humanoid avian with huge feathered, insectoid, cloth, or metallic wings at the DM's choice.

consts.name: ddyAirCoinPct
consts.comment: the Air treasure rule: only a 10% chance that the lair of a creature of elemental Air in its home plane contains coinage - if a coinage treasure type is called for, replace it with containers of perfumes and other interesting scents of equal value.

consts.name: ddyFireCoinPct
consts.comment: the Fire treasure rule: a 20% chance of coinage in this realm, the coins melted into solid blocks of equivalent weight and value; if coinage is not found, the treasure is rare woods, coal, textiles and other burnables, protected from the flames.

consts.name: ddyParaTreasureChance
consts.comment: the para- and quasi-elemental treasure rule: the para-elemental planes are treated as one of the two major planes they border (50% chance of each); of the quasi-elementals, seven of the eight take treasure according to their aligned major plane - Vacuum the exception, with normal treasure; and treasure that could be harmed by its surroundings (magical scrolls in the plane of Fire) is protected if the creature has at least low intelligence.

bools.name: ddyAnalogueDoctrine
bools.comment: the analogue doctrine: the inner planes are natural environments to their inhabitants much like the regions of the Prime - elemental herbivores taking sustenance from their surroundings, elemental carnivores preying on other elemental (and normative) life; the DM runs encounters with modified stats from the Monster Manual, Monster Manual II, and Fiend Folio. The no-analogue list: creatures native to the Ethereal, Astral or outer planes (slaad, githyanki, devils) have no elemental analogues; there are no elemental undead (though Prime planar undead may be found in the inner planes); and the PC humanoids (humans, elves, dwarves, gnomes, halflings, orcs and their mixed breeds) have none - there are no elemental wizards, though there are elemental creatures that can cast spells.

bools.name: ddyStatModsRule
bools.comment: the stat modifications: frequency unchanged, number appearing unchanged, armor class unchanged unless noted, movement tripled for Air/Smoke/Steam and doubled for Water, number of attacks and damage unchanged, magic resistance standard, intelligence unchanged, alignment unchanged or neutral with tendencies toward the standard; the lair percentage - elemental creatures in their native planes 10% less likely to be in lair than Prime creatures, those inhabiting pockets of their native element in other planes 10% more likely; and psionic ability none unless specifically noted for the creature.

bools.name: ddyElementAbilitiesRule
bools.comment: the general abilities of inner-planar creatures: they move through their plane and those that directly adjoin it (the para- and quasi-planes for a major-element native) as Prime travelers move through the Ethereal; they can see into the Border Ethereal; and they can enter the Ethereal from the inner planes - but unless otherwise noted they cannot travel from the Ethereal into a Prime Material, or even into a Prime's Border Ethereal, without outside help. The per-element summary: Air immune to wind, weather, lightning and cloud spells but affected by vacuum; Fire immune to heat and flame, affected by cold- and water-based spells; Earth immune to earth-modifying spells, AC improved one factor, can passwall; Water immune to water-control spells, affected by fire, breathes water and blends with surroundings; Smoke immune to air- and fire-based attacks and asphyxiation; Magma immune to fire and earth, can passwall; Ooze immune to earth- and water-based spells, can passwall; Ice immune to cold, air and water attacks, can passwall through ice; Lightning immune to air, weather and electricity; Radiance unaffected by fire, heat and light, vulnerable to darkness, water and cold; Minerals unaffected by solid-matter spells, can passwall; Steam immune to heat, cold, air and water magic; Vacuum immune to vacuum and negative energy, vulnerable to air; Ash immune to cold and negative energy, vulnerable to warmth; Dust immune to earth-affecting spells and negative energy; Salt unaffected by fire and heat, vulnerable to water - and where a Prime creature's immunity is a vulnerability for the analogue (an elemental fire giant in the plane of Ash), the analogue retains the immunity.

bools.name: ddySizeChangeRule
bools.comment: the size-change table (the DM's spur-of-the-moment appearance guide): Air-family (smoke, dust, vacuum, ash, steam) - smaller by 2 on 1-10, smaller by 1 on 1-10 past that... as printed: smaller by 2 at 1-10 and smaller by 1 at 1-10 with same at 11-40, larger by 1 at 41-90, larger by 2 at 91-00; Fire family (lightning, radiance, salt) - smaller by 2 at 1-10, smaller by 1 at 11-25, same at 26-75, larger by 1 at 76-90, larger by 2 at 91-00; Earth family (minerals, ice) - smaller by 2 at 1-30, smaller by 1 at 31-60, same at 61-90, larger by 1 at 91-00; Water family (magma, ooze) - smaller by 2 at 1-5, smaller by 1 at 6-10, same at 11-90, larger by 1 at 91-95, larger by 2 at 96-00. The effects: smaller by 1 or 2 reduces size by one or two factors (L to M, M to S), an S creature halved again per factor (a three-foot being at smaller-by-2 is nine inches); larger by 1 or 2 increases by the factors, an L creature doubled and if necessary doubled again - a 15-foot giant might have a 60-foot elemental equivalent.

bools.name: ddyFireAppearanceRule
bools.comment: the Fire appearances: 1-30 a sharply defined flaming solid (cube, tetrahedron, octahedron) with flaming arms from the center; 31-35 a collection of 2d6 small geometric solids orbiting a central solid, the orbiters removable without harm; 36-45 a flaming humanoid form with the Prime counterpart's general facial features; 46-50 a flaming humanoid with humanoid features; 51-90 a flaming form resembling the Prime counterpart; 91-00 a solid fiery counterpart with a shining metallic hide radiating the color of the nearby flames.

bools.name: ddyEarthWaterAppearanceRule
bools.comment: the Earth and Water appearances: Earth - 1-10 a roughly spherical boulder with oozing appendages; 11-30 a stone statue of the counterpart (polished black or amber to roughly-hewn grey or brown); 31-35 the statue with humanoid shape and counterpart features (a man with a beholder's head); 36-70 a tripedal xorn-like form with three or more arms and legs and jaws atop the body; 71-90 a crystalline counterpart that shatters into useless shards on death; 91-95 the crystalline form with humanoid shape and features; 96-00 a rough formless crystal mass with appendages from the center. Water - creatures tending to blend with their aquatic surroundings: 1-10 an amoeboid blob with oozing appendages; 11-25 a serpentine form with the counterpart's general features; 26-60 a fish-like mer-creature (the foreparts of the creature, the hind parts of a fish, such as the triton); 91-00 entirely fish-like, additional features only when they affect the creature's powers. And the para- and quasi-appearances: the para-elementals split between humanoid and counterpart forms - Smoke humanoid on 1-20, Magma 1-25, Ooze 1-40, Ice 1-10, the counterpart on the rest; the lightning quasi-elemental a ball or oblong of energy with leg-like bolts, radiance a colored sphere of force, mineral a delicate insectoid counterpart, steam as the smoke forms, vacuum a sphere of invisible force, ash a grey duplicate collapsing into ash when slain, dust a cloud or whirlwind, salt a white salt-encrusted duplicate.

bools.name: ddyTreasureRule
bools.comment: the treasure of elemental creatures: the lairs contain treasure as noted for their counterparts in the monster books, the exact nature varying from plane to plane - Air at 10% coinage with perfumes and scents of equal value substituted; Fire at 20% with coins melted into blocks of equivalent weight and value, else rare woods, coal, textiles and other burnables protected from the flames; Earth collecting more metallic treasure than gems and jewelry, jewelry replaced by a similar number of gems; Water normal coinage with potions doubled; the para-planes 50/50 between their two bordering majors; the quasi-planes seven of eight by their aligned major with Vacuum normal; treasure harmable by its surroundings (scrolls in Fire) protected by creatures of at least low intelligence; and lairs in elemental pockets or regions duplicating other inner planes treated as if in those planes.
